edge: Use several directly nested alternatives with one shared name.
positive: Give if and else alternatives the same block name and select each in separate elaborations.

edge: Make the conflicting block unselected.
negative: Reuse a name across separate generate constructs or an ordinary declaration.
positive: Use distinct names across separate constructs and declarations.

negative: Reference a name belonging only to an unselected alternative.
positive: Hierarchically reference a declaration through the selected named block.

positive: Select one alternative with a constant parameter.

positive: Reference a declaration from within the unnamed block's instantiated hierarchy.

positive: Build unbracketed if–else-if and mixed if/case schemes whose alternatives share a block name.

edge: Conflict with a zero-instance array declaration.
negative: Reuse a variable or generated-array name.
positive: Use distinct names.

edge: Nest conditional and loop generate constructs.
positive: Place a nested generate construct and other allowed module items in a generate block.

edge: Reference an enclosing declaration from a nested generate block.
positive: Directly reference an enclosing variable from inside a generate block.

positive: Use ordinary declarations in a generate block.

positive: Select a block containing a declaration, behavior, and module instance and observe them under its hierarchy.

negative: Mutate required delimiters or production ordering one at a time.

positive: Exercise each generate construct production in a minimal valid context.

positive: Use nested unbracketed if-generates and select values that distinguish nearest-if association.

negative: Use an item admitted only by another context's generate-item category.
positive: Use a context-appropriate generate item in each of module, interface, and checker.

edge: Use it in a nested generate construct.
negative: Attempt to override a parameter declared within a generate block.
positive: Declare and use a parameter in an instantiated generate block.

negative: Omit endgenerate.
positive: Close a generate region with endgenerate.

positive: Use one generate region directly in a module.

positive: Compare equivalent modules with and without a generate/endgenerate wrapper around the same conditional generate construct and observe the same selected hierarchy and values.

edge: Use dependent parameters in the constant expression.
negative: Control a scheme with a runtime variable.
positive: Control a scheme with a parameter-based constant expression.
